newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says debate on EMU start, rules not helpful.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says debate on EMU start, rules not helpful.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday the current debate about European economic and monetary union (EMU) was not helping the country's effort to qualify for the launch of the single currency.
Kohl added that he himself was confident Germany would fulfil the criteria and that the EMU timetable could be met.

"The prevailing discussions about the interpretations of the criteria, timetable or number of participants (is) not helpful," Kohl said according to a text of a speech he was to deliver at a Bavarian entrepreneur conference.
Instead of debating aspects of the euro, Germany should concentrate on its own efforts to qualify for the planned launch in January 1999, he said.
Bonn needs to cut its gaping budget deficit to meet the requirement that public deficits total no more than three percent of gross domestic product.
Kohl has clashed recently with Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber, who has called for delaying the euro unless participating nations meet a strict interpretation of the entry criteria.
